\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مرگ} (marg)}{مرگ (marg)}]{\fa{مرگ} (marg) — death}

\label{lesson:FA-C337-marg}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an orphan, then the Persian for custody.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مرگ}}
\textbf{\fa{مرگ}} (\emph{marg}) — \textquotedblleft{}death\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{مرگ} \fa{پدرش} \fa{به} \fa{شهر} \fa{برگشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ba'd az marg-e pedarash be shahr bargasht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After his father's death he went back to the city.
\end{quote}

Plain and strong; in polite speech people say \emph{dargozasht} or \emph{fowt}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{marg} is a native Persian word, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{marg}, \textquotedblleft{}death\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marg}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{marg}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an orphan, then the Persian for custody, then say \emph{marg} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{درگذشتن} (dargozashtan)}{درگذشتن (dargozashtan)}]{\fa{درگذشتن} (dargozashtan) — to pass away}

\label{lesson:FA-C337-dargozashtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for custody, then the Persian for death.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{درگذشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{درگذشتن}} (\emph{dargozashtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to pass away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادربزرگم} \fa{سال} \fa{گذشته} \fa{درگذشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdarbozorgam sâl-e gozashte dargozasht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother passed away last year.
\end{quote}

Respectful. Present stem \emph{gozar-}: \emph{dar migozarad}. The noun is \emph{dargozasht} \textquotedblleft{}a passing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dargozashtan} is the native verb \emph{gozashtan} \textquotedblleft{}to pass\textquotedblright{} with the prefix \emph{dar}: to pass on. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dargozashtan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dargozashtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dargozashtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for custody, then the Persian for death, then say \emph{dargozashtan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فوت} \fa{کردن} (fowt kardan)}{فوت کردن (fowt kardan)}]{\fa{فوت} \fa{کردن} (fowt kardan) — to die (formal), to pass on}

\label{lesson:FA-C337-fowt-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for death, then the Persian for to pass away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فوت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{فوت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{fowt kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to die (formal), to pass on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همسایه} \fa{ما} \fa{دیروز} \fa{فوت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hamsâye-ye mâ diruz fowt kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our neighbour died yesterday.
\end{quote}

Neutral and polite, common in notices. Present \emph{fowt mikonad}; the noun \emph{fowt} is \textquotedblleft{}a death\textquotedblright{}. Spelled the same, \emph{fut kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to blow\textquotedblright{} is a different word.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fowt} \textquotedblleft{}death, a passing\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{fawt}, \textquotedblleft{}a passing, a loss\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fowt kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fowt kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fowt kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for death, then the Persian for to pass away, then say \emph{fowt kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دفن} \fa{کردن} (dafn kardan)}{دفن کردن (dafn kardan)}]{\fa{دفن} \fa{کردن} (dafn kardan) — to bury}

\label{lesson:FA-C337-dafn-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to pass away, then the Persian for to die.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دفن} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{دفن} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{dafn kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to bury\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{روستای} \fa{خودش} \fa{دفن} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U râ dar rustâ-ye khodash dafn kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They buried him in his own village.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{dafn mikonad}; the passive is \emph{dafn shod}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dafn} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{dafn}, \textquotedblleft{}burial\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word). \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قبر} (qabr)}{قبر (qabr)}]{\fa{قبر} (qabr) — a grave}

\label{lesson:FA-C337-qabr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to die, then the Persian for to bury.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قبر}}
\textbf{\fa{قبر}} (\emph{qabr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a grave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هر} \fa{پنجشنبه} \fa{سر} \fa{قبر} \fa{پدرش} \fa{میرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Har panjshanbe sar-e qabr-e pedarash miraft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every Thursday he used to go to his father's grave.
\end{quote}

Broken plural \emph{qobur}. Thursday is the usual day for visiting graves.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qabr} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{qabr}, \textquotedblleft{}grave\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
